review_request.range_note: The range 6fbd8a459d763b0fb58b165e0e99f16303ba2c97..revision starts at the task admission commit.

findings.claim: A bare command names its caller with bindingAgentId, which trusts the pane that TMUX and TMUX_PANE name without the ancestry proof TM-234 added (callerRunsInPane). For integrate and record-landing this is harmless, because requireGranteeCaller still proves the caller. For admit, start-worker, stop-worker and report, though, a process with no AO_AGENT_ID can set TMUX_PANE to the lead's pane and be named as the lead (owner falls back to env.AO_AGENT_ID). That is no weaker than the old self-set AO_AGENT_ID, but the helper looks like identity proof.
findings.evidence: bindingAgentId calls resolveBinding and then matches the census with sameBinding, and never calls callerRunsInPane. cli.mjs sets env.AO_AGENT_ID from it and derives owner from env.TM_SESSION_ID || env.AO_AGENT_ID.
findings.fix: Call callerRunsInPane(here) inside bindingAgentId (return null when it is false or unreadable), so a bare command is named only from the pane it actually runs in.

findings.claim: The criterion-2 test checks the documented commands against ruleMatches, which is this module's own model of Claude Code's Bash(<prefix> *) matching, not Claude Code itself. Criterion 4 (a live auto-mode check in a temporary repo showing a delegated lead's record-landing, admit and finish report run without a prompt) has no evidence in the request. So nothing here shows that the real harness accepts the Bash(... *) rule form as written.
findings.evidence: ruleMatches is used only by topology-permissions.test.mjs. The request includes no live-check transcript or test output.
findings.fix: Attach the live auto-mode check output (lead with a grant: no prompt; non-delegated session: refused by ao-topology) as task evidence before landing.

findings.claim: Criterion 1 names the project .claude/settings.json, but the implementation writes <lead agent dir>/.claude/settings.local.json. The deviation is sound, since only the lead reads that file and workers never do, and it is documented, but the criterion was not amended. The CHANGELOG also doesn't flag that this is uncommitted, machine-local state that needs an ignore rule.
findings.evidence: leadSettingsTarget returns join(session.cwd, '.claude', 'settings.local.json'). The docs say to keep it out of git with a **/.claude/settings.local.json ignore rule, but the patch adds no such rule.
findings.fix: Amend TM-243 criterion 1 to the lead-local file, and add the **/.claude/settings.local.json ignore rule (or have install check that it is ignored).

findings.claim: The rest is sound. Install and uninstall are operator-only through the shared gate. The rule list is exactly the approved one; MCP names are validated with no wildcards; merge, push and deploy are never written. Install prints the diff, is idempotent (byte-identical second run) and preserves other keys. Uninstall removes only the ledgered rules. A shared launch directory (TM-242) is refused. Dispatched workers are refused lead verbs at the CLI. The rules grant no authority, and tests cover a lead with and without a grant, an expired grant, and worker cases on both verbs. The TM_DISPATCH_WORKER guard is marker-based (the stated same-user limit). This branch and TM-248 (e357d4d) both refactor requireNoAgentSession, so expect a merge conflict there.
